Photograph: KCNA via KNS/AFP/Getty Images Russia-Ukraine war at a glance Ukraine Explainer Ukraine war briefing: North Korea sending 50,000 troops to Russia – Zelenskyy Kim Jong-un’s regime has already provided thousands of soldiers, as well as missiles and artillery; Turkey readies arms package for Ukraine. What we know on day 1,629 Warren Murray and agencies Sun 9 Aug 2026 21.18 EDT Last modified on Sun 9 Aug 2026 21.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Up to 50,000 North Korean soldiers will be deployed in Russia , Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, while calling on South Korea to provide support for Ukraine’s air defence. It is an increase from the estimated 30,000 announced by the Ukrainian president in July. Kyiv had found some North Korean missiles in Ukraine’s territory, he said. “It is absolutely clear that ⁠North Korea will continue to build its experience in modern warfare, receive licences from Russia, and receive all ​kinds of military tools from them.” This month, an official at Ukraine’s military intelligence told Reuters that a North Korean missile unit has begun deploying personnel and equipment to western Russia and the unit could be equipped with 120 ballistic ⁠missiles and six launchers for strikes against Ukraine. North Korea sent an estimated 14,000 soldiers to Russia’s Kursk region in 2024, helping Moscow fight an invasion by Ukrainian forces. Thousands have been wounded or killed . North Korea has supplied ​Russia with millions ‌of artillery and mortar rounds – sometimes of dangerously low quality, according to Russian milbloggers and troops – ​as well as ballistic missiles, long-range ​artillery and multiple-launch rocket systems, according to Ukrainian and independent assessments. Zelenskyy continued that Ukraine “would very much like to receive support from South Korea in ‌an area where we have a shortage”, referring to air defence systems . “We are ready to work on the drone deal and other areas as well,” he said, adding that Ukrainian diplomats “are in contact” with Seoul to push potential deals. Ukraine is very short of high-end ​air defences and Russia has ​tried to exploit this by using ​more ballistic missiles, which are very hard to shoot down without interceptors like the US-owned Patriot. Seventy Atacms short-range ballistic missiles are part of a weapons package that Ukraine is poised to buy from Turkey , according to US congressional documents (pdf) . The US would have to approve the resale of the American-origin weapons. The state department indicated to Congress it is prepared to give permission. Along with the M39 Atacms missiles, Turkey also plans to sell Kyiv 47,000 artillery rounds, 12 M270 multiple-launch rocket systems (MLRS) and more than 2,000 cluster bombs, according to the notice from the US state department. Russian missiles struck a high-rise apartment block in the Saltivskyi district of Kharkiv, killing two people and injuring 13 , said regional head Oleh Syniehubov. Zelenskyy said eight people were wounded in Odesa, where strikes damaged the power grid, the port and residential buildings. He condemned an “absolutely brutal” strike targeting energy infrastructure near a shopping centre in Pavlohrad, Dnipropetrovsk region , that wounded nine people including four children. Russia said Ukrainian drones killed five people and injured two dozen others in the Belgorod region. Zelenskyy, in his evening address on Sunday, defended Ukraine’s replies to Russia’s attacks – including strikes on Russian oil refineries, air defence systems and radar stations – as “truly just responses”. “The Russian war will be increasingly felt at home, in Russia,” he said. The World Health Organization chief, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, said a WHO warehouse stocking medical supplies in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro was destroyed in strikes on Friday. “I cannot say loudly enough: attacks on health care must stop. Otherwise, people are deprived of lifesaving healthcare,” Tedros posted. “Even wars have rules. One of those is that health must be protected!” Ukrainian drone strikes damaged commercial sites and a home in the Russian city of Novorossiysk, said the mayor, Andrey Kravchenko. A major fuel terminal is located at Novorossiysk that links Kazakhstan’s oilfields to markets around the world. It has previously been a target for Ukrainian strikes. Bulgaria summoned Ukraine’s ambassador after a drone entered Bulgarian airspace , the country’s public broadcaster BNT reported on Sunday. The drone exploded on Saturday close to an international gas pipeline shortly after crossing the border from Romania, the Bulgarians said. No casualties or damage were reported. Bulgaria’s defence ministry said the incident was likely accidental and involved a drone that appeared to be a Ukrainian type. Kyiv’s foreign ministry said Ukraine did not deliberately target Bulgaria and the two sides were in “close contact” about it. A “powerful explosion” believed to be from a combat drone was reported in the village of Crocmaz, in south-east Moldova near the border with Ukraine, local police said on Sunday. No one was injured by the impact, which caused a vegetation fire in the Stefan Voda district, police said, adding that “fragments of a combat drone were found at the scene” and would be examined by specialists. Police did not specify the origin of the drone. The UK defence secretary, Wes Streeting, has urged allies to boost Ukraine’s air defences ahead of a winter that Vladimir Putin will seek to use as a “weapon” against Kyiv. Writing in the Sunday Times, Streeting warned that while Putin was currently losing the war, “Ukrainians know what winter brings, and how it can change the picture”. Allies’ efforts to assist Ukraine “must include greater resources for air defence”. “My task – alongside my German counterpart Boris Pistorius, with whom I co-chair the Ukraine defence contact group – is to turn the goodwill of some 50 nations into concrete help.” Pope Leo on Sunday said innocent people were being ⁠killed and wounded in Ukraine and Russia, and called for an end to ⁠the conflict. “Tragic incidents ⁠are ​multiplying, causing an ever-growing number of civilian victims, including children,” the pontiff said before worshippers ⁠gathered for Sunday’s Angelus prayer. “I renew my heartfelt appeal for international humanitarian law to be ⁠respected and for attacks against civilian targets to cease on ​both sides.” More than ‌16,000 civilians have been killed, according to the UN, the overwhelming majority of them Ukrainian . https://www.politico.eu/article/donald-t.text: Denmark and Iceland pushed back Tuesday after U.S. President Donald Trump posted a map folding Greenland and Iceland into the United States, while French politicians also protested after territories belonging to France appeared under the American flag. Trump posted the image on his Truth Social platform on Monday without explanation. Canada, Greenland, Iceland, Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean were daubed in the U.S. flag and labeled “United States of America.” Trump has repeatedly talked about taking control of Greenland and repeatedly floated turning Canada into America’s 51st state. Advertisement Advertisement “It’s disturbing and, in many ways, completely inappropriate,” Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen told broadcaster DR. “It’s obviously a sign that the U.S. president still harbors some kind of maximalist vision in his own mind. We need to rein that in.” Icelandic Foreign Minister Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir summoned U.S. Ambassador Billy Long on Tuesday, with her ministry saying it made clear that the post was “entirely inappropriate.” The U.S. president has also repeatedly mixed up Iceland, a sovereign country, and Greenland, a self-governing Danish overseas territory. At the World Economic Forum in Davos in January, he referred to Iceland four times while discussing issues relating to Greenland, including blaming “Iceland” for a drop in U.S. stock markets. Trump’s map also included French, British and Dutch territory. The French Caribbean and Saint-Pierre and Miquelon, off Canada’s coast, were covered by the U.S. flag. Left-wing presidential hopeful Jean-Luc Mélenchon said Macron should “send the aircraft carrier to maintain control over our sovereignty and reassure the populations under threat.” Conservative politician Xavier Bertrand was more restrained in an X post on Wednesday: “Our sovereignty is not reshaped by a series of edited posts on social media.” The latest post landed as European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visited Greenland on Monday, declaring the island was making a “clear choice” to deepen ties with Europe and unveiling a €200 million investment package. The star-spangled map was part of a wider burst of Truth Social posts over recent weeks in which Trump claimed Apple Maps had joined Google Maps in renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America,” declaring the change “complete, ratified, and binding.” Advertisement Advertisement During the holiday-weekend splurge, he posted a ranking of U.S. presidents with himself at the top, along with pictures generated by artificial intelligence depicting sunken Iranian ships. He has also posted AI-generated images depicting himself as Superman , Green Lantern and a Christ-like figure . Victor Goury-Laffont contributed to this report.

https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2.text: Nathan Pinnock-James: ‘TikTok has really opened the door to really niche, specific topics coming on to your “for you” page.’ Photograph: @networknathan Instagram View image in fullscreen Nathan Pinnock-James: ‘TikTok has really opened the door to really niche, specific topics coming on to your “for you” page.’ Photograph: @networknathan Instagram TikTok All aboard the TrainTok trend: spotters and staff boost rail content online Number of videos about British trains doubles in three months as creators find audiences interested in workings of railways George Francis Lee Sun 25 Oct 2026 10.00 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google They are not just gathered at the end of your local train station platform any more. Now they are on your social media platforms too. Trainspotters have played a part in more than doubling the number of videos about British trains on TikTok in the last three months. According to the platform, the rise in rail content is also down to more people seeking information on cheap tickets, facts about the London Underground and tales from train staff. Posts tagged with #UKTrains have increased by 247% over recent months. The trend has even led to train staff moonlighting as content creators. Shamal Cain, who goes by the handle Tube Bellingham, is a Transport for London employee who shares advice for commuters across the capital. According to Cain, scrollers are keen to learn more about topics they know little about but that affect their daily lives. “I realised how many people use London transport but don’t actually know a lot of information about it,” he said. Cain said many commuters were not fully aware of the TfL journey planner or how to avoid penalty fares from not tapping in and out. After noticing the gap, he thought: “Why don’t I just record giving information on what I do?” He said: “A majority of people commute through TfL. I think because a lot of people are doing that on a daily basis, they’re very engaged with information.” When Cain joined TikTok, direct messages came in fast, with followers asking him about alternative routes when services were down or for advice on getting a job with TfL. The popularity of train content has also risen thanks to enthusiast rail influencers such as Nathan Pinnock-James, who makes educational transport videos. “Since I started posting on TikTok, there’s been a lot of people that have the context of what a train is, how to use a train, but may not have noticed certain aspects of it,” said Pinnock-James, AKA Network Nathan. “They’re like: ‘Oh, wow! That’s quite shocking!’” He said obscure hobbies thrived on the app. “TikTok has really opened the door to really niche, specific topics coming on to your ‘for you’ page. It’s allowed people to find things that they didn’t know were interesting to them.” The 24-year-old said he found an audience online by creating videos about the best trainspotting locations, station openings, and explainers on how the shape of train wheels make DLR carriages wobble. Yazmin How, the head of emerging communities at TikTok UK, said: “It’s inspiring to see such a wide variety of creators, whether it’s professional train drivers, tube historians, young enthusiasts or comedy creators, using short-form video to make transport content entertaining and accessible to everyone. “The growth we’re seeing in #traintok reflects a real appetite among our UK community for authentic, educational storytelling that connects people, turning everyday travel into a shared community interest.” View image in fullscreen Francis Bourgeois found popularity on TikTok in 2021. Photograph: Alex Lake/The Observer Short video content about trains, sometimes called TrainTok, has been a growing part of the social media app for years. The media personality Francis Bourgeois found popularity on TikTok in 2021 after his videos of him reacting to British locomotives went viral. While human creators are jumping onboard, AI-generated videos – including clips that show high-speed trains and passengers falling out of tube carriages – are also contributing to the growth. In late 2025, TikTok revealed that more than 1bn videos that included AI were hosted on its application. The company said its content operations team “works closely with creators and publishers to support the flow of high-quality content in the TikTok ecosystem”. TikTok, which announced the increase in train content during an annual trend report at its UK headquarters, said there was a growing interest in niche topics across its platform. It said searches about history in the UK had gone up by 50% in the last six months, and posts about the National Trust had doubled during the same period.
